definitionEn: A food made from flour, water and yeast, baked in an oven.
example: She bought fresh bread from the bakery near the station this morning.

definitionEn: A small white or brown grain that is cooked and eaten as a staple food.
example: Rice is eaten at almost every meal in our family's home.

definitionEn: The flesh of animals used as food, such as beef, pork or chicken.
example: He doesn't eat much meat, so he cooks lots of vegetables instead.

definitionEn: A cold-blooded animal that lives in water and is eaten as food.
example: We grilled the fish with lemon and herbs for a light dinner.

definitionEn: The oval object laid by birds and some other animals, often eaten as food.
example: She cracked two eggs into the bowl and whisked them together.

definitionEn: A solid food made from milk, often yellow or white and with a strong taste.
example: The pizza was topped with melted cheese and fresh tomatoes.

definitionEn: A white liquid produced by cows and other animals, drunk as a drink.
example: Every morning, the children drink a glass of warm milk before school.

definitionEn: A sweet substance obtained from plants, used to sweeten food and drinks.
example: Too much sugar in drinks can harm your teeth over many years.

definitionEn: A white mineral used to season food and to preserve it.
example: The cook added a pinch of salt to bring out the flavour.

definitionEn: A liquid food made by boiling vegetables, meat or fish in water or stock.
example: My grandmother makes a delicious vegetable soup every winter.

definitionEn: To cook food in hot oil or fat in a pan.
example: She fried the onions until they turned soft and golden brown.

definitionEn: To cook food under or over direct heat, usually on a metal rack.
example: We grilled sausages and vegetables on the barbecue in the garden.

definitionEn: To heat a liquid until it bubbles and turns into steam.
example: Boil the pasta for ten minutes until it is soft but firm.

definitionEn: To cook food in an oven using dry heat, such as bread or cakes.
example: I baked a chocolate cake for my sister's birthday party yesterday.

definitionEn: To cook food, especially meat or vegetables, in an oven with fat.
example: They roasted a whole chicken with garlic and herbs for Sunday lunch.

definitionEn: To cook food by exposing it to rising hot vapour from boiling water.
example: She steamed the broccoli gently so it kept its bright green colour.

definitionEn: To cut food into smaller pieces with a knife.
example: Chop the garlic finely before adding it to the hot oil.

definitionEn: To add salt, pepper or herbs to food to improve its flavour.
example: Season the soup with pepper and taste it before serving to guests.

definitionEn: The distinctive taste of a food or drink.
example: The sauce has a rich flavour that comes from slow cooking.

definitionEn: Containing strong spices that give a hot or peppery taste.
example: The spicy noodles made my eyes water, but I loved every bite.

definitionEn: Having a sharp, acidic taste like that of lemons.
example: The sauce tasted sour, so she added a spoon of honey.

definitionEn: Having a sharp, unpleasant taste, like black coffee or some greens.
example: The bitter coffee needed plenty of sugar to make it pleasant.

definitionEn: Firm, dry and easily broken, especially when freshly cooked.
example: The toast was crisp on the outside and soft on the inside.

definitionEn: Easy to cut or chew, not tough, especially after cooking.
example: The beef was so tender that it fell apart with a fork.

definitionEn: A set of instructions for preparing a dish, with a list of ingredients.
example: My mother shared her favourite recipe for spring rolls with me.

definitionEn: One of the foods that are combined to make a particular dish.
example: The key ingredient in the dish is fresh lemongrass from the garden.

definitionEn: A style of cooking characteristic of a particular country or region.
example: Vietnamese cuisine is known for its fresh herbs and balanced flavours.

definitionEn: A rare or expensive food regarded as especially fine or delicious.
example: Snails are considered a delicacy in parts of France and Spain.

definitionEn: Cooked food bought from a shop to be eaten elsewhere.
example: We ordered a takeaway curry because nobody wanted to cook.

definitionEn: A small amount of food eaten between main meals.
example: He ate a small snack of crackers and cheese before the afternoon class.

definitionEn: Food that remains uneaten after a meal and is kept for later.
example: We reheated the leftovers from last night's dinner for lunch today.

definitionEn: To soak food in a seasoned liquid to add flavour before cooking.
example: Marinate the chicken overnight so the spices penetrate the meat fully.

definitionEn: To cook gently in liquid just below boiling point.
example: Let the stew simmer slowly for two hours until the beef is tender.

definitionEn: To cook meat or vegetables slowly in a small amount of liquid in a covered pot.
example: The chef braised the lamb shanks in red wine until they fell from the bone.

definitionEn: To plunge food briefly into boiling water and then into cold water.
example: Blanch the green beans for two minutes to keep their bright colour.

definitionEn: To change through the action of yeast or bacteria, producing alcohol or acid.
example: The cabbage was left to ferment in brine for several weeks.

definitionEn: To preserve food by soaking it in vinegar, brine or another acidic liquid.
example: She pickled cucumbers and carrots in vinegar to store them through winter.

definitionEn: To steep ingredients in liquid so that their flavour passes into it.
example: Infuse the tea with fresh mint leaves for five minutes before pouring.

definitionEn: To decorate a dish with small pieces of food to make it look appealing.
example: The waiter garnished each plate with fresh coriander and lime wedges.

definitionEn: To coat food with a shiny liquid such as syrup, egg or sauce before cooking.
example: Glaze the ham with honey and mustard during the last half hour of roasting.

definitionEn: To beat ingredients rapidly until they are light and frothy.
example: Whisk the egg whites until they form stiff, glossy peaks.

definitionEn: To press and fold dough with the hands so it becomes smooth and elastic.
example: Knead the dough for ten minutes until it springs back when pressed.

definitionEn: To brown the surface of food quickly over very high heat.
example: Sear the steak in a very hot pan to lock in its juices.

definitionEn: To mix two liquids that do not normally blend, such as oil and vinegar.
example: Whisking the oil slowly helps to emulsify the mayonnaise into a smooth sauce.

definitionEn: To heat sugar or food until it turns golden brown and develops a sweet taste.
example: Caramelise the onions slowly over low heat until they turn deep brown.

definitionEn: Having a strong, pleasant smell, often from herbs or spices.
example: The aromatic curry filled the whole kitchen with warm spicy smells.

definitionEn: Having a strong, sharp smell or taste that is quite powerful.
example: The pungent smell of garlic and ginger drifted from the kitchen.

definitionEn: Having a salty or spicy flavour rather than a sweet one.
example: She prefers savoury snacks like crackers and cheese to sweet biscuits.

definitionEn: Juicy, tender and full of flavour, especially meat or fruit.
example: The succulent peaches were sweet, soft and dripping with juice.

meaningVi: tươi mát, có vị chua thơm
definitionEn: Having a fresh, sharp, lively flavour, often from citrus peel.
example: A zesty lemon dressing brightened the simple green salad.

meaningVi: cay nồng, kích thích vị giác
definitionEn: Pleasantly sharp or spicy in taste, stimulating the palate.
example: The piquant sauce added a lively kick to the grilled fish.

definitionEn: Pleasant enough in taste to be eaten or drunk with enjoyment.
example: The medicine tasted bitter, but the honey made it palatable for children.

definitionEn: The feel of food in the mouth, such as crispy, smooth or chewy.
example: I love the contrast of crunchy texture against creamy soft filling.

definitionEn: The distinctive aroma of a wine, or a pleasant fragrance of food.
example: The wine has a delicate bouquet of berries and vanilla.

definitionEn: The sense of taste, or a person's ability to appreciate flavours.
example: The chef has a refined palate and can detect every subtle spice.

definitionEn: The art and science of good eating, especially of fine food.
example: The festival celebrates the rich gastronomy of the Mekong Delta region.

definitionEn: Relating to cooking or the kitchen.
example: She trained for three years to develop her culinary skills in Paris.

definitionEn: A person who enjoys fine food and is an expert in judging it.
example: The gourmet travelled across three continents to taste the finest dishes.

definitionEn: A shop selling prepared foods, cheeses and imported specialities.
example: We bought cold cuts and olives from the delicatessen on the corner.

definitionEn: A supply of food and other necessities, especially for a journey.
example: The hikers packed enough provisions to last them through the week.

definitionEn: A basic food that forms a large part of people's regular diet.
example: Noodles are a staple of the daily diet across much of Asia.

definitionEn: Something served alongside a main dish to complement it.
example: Steamed vegetables make a light accompaniment to the rich roast beef.

definitionEn: A substance such as sauce or spice added to food to enhance its flavour.
example: Fish sauce is an essential condiment in many Vietnamese kitchens.

definitionEn: A thin soup made by boiling meat, fish or vegetables in water.
example: The chicken broth was clear, warm and gently seasoned with ginger.

definitionEn: A flavoured liquid made by simmering bones or vegetables, used as a base for soups.
example: Use homemade stock for the soup to give it a deeper flavour.

definitionEn: A sweet dish or sweet food, such as a candy, cake or pastry.
example: The bakery's elegant confections drew queues of customers every weekend.

definitionEn: The chemical process in which sugar is converted into alcohol or acid by microbes.
example: Fermentation gives the kimchi its tangy flavour and distinctive smell.

definitionEn: A mixture of liquids that do not normally blend, held together in fine droplets.
example: The vinaigrette is a stable emulsion of oil, vinegar and mustard.

definitionEn: A sauce made by boiling liquid until it thickens and its flavour concentrates.
example: The chef spooned a rich wine reduction over the seared duck breast.

definitionEn: A wide variety of different foods offered together at one meal.
example: The hotel served a generous smorgasbord of breakfast dishes every morning.

definitionEn: A savoury taste associated with glutamate, found in foods such as seaweed and cheese.
example: Dried mushrooms add a deep umami richness to the broth.

definitionEn: A pleasantly sharp or spicy quality that stimulates the taste buds.
example: The lime juice added an unexpected piquancy to the creamy sauce.

definitionEn: To enjoy a taste or experience slowly and with great pleasure.
example: She savoured every mouthful of the rich chocolate dessert.

definitionEn: Relating to the sense of taste or the process of tasting food.
example: The restaurant designed each course to delight the gustatory senses.

definitionEn: Relating to the sense of smell and the way odours are detected.
example: The bakery's olfactory charm drew passers-by in from the street.

definitionEn: Safe and suitable to be eaten by people.
example: Only the flowers and young leaves of this plant are edible.

definitionEn: Not pleasant to taste, or unacceptable to the mind.
example: The overcooked vegetables were so unpalatable that nobody finished them.

definitionEn: Lacking flavour or interest, dull and uninspiring.
example: The insipid soup needed salt, pepper and a squeeze of lime.

definitionEn: Having little flavour or interest, mild and unexciting.
example: The hospital food was bland, so the patients added extra herbs themselves.

definitionEn: Excessively sweet, or unpleasantly sentimental in style.
example: The dessert was so saccharine that a single spoonful was enough.

definitionEn: Sharp or bitter in taste, causing the mouth to feel dry and puckered.
example: The astringent red wine left a dry, puckering feeling on the tongue.

definitionEn: Having a sharp, bitter smell or taste that stings the nose or throat.
example: The acrid smoke from the burnt toast filled the small flat.

definitionEn: Having an unpleasant smell or taste because the fat has gone bad.
example: The butter had turned rancid, so we threw the whole packet away.

definitionEn: Decaying and giving off an extremely foul and unpleasant smell.
example: The putrid fish had been left out in the sun for two days.

definitionEn: Thick and sticky, flowing slowly like syrup or honey.
example: The viscous caramel clung to the spoon as it slowly dripped down.

definitionEn: Having a thick, jelly-like consistency when cooked or set.
example: The broth turned gelatinous after simmering overnight with pork bones.

definitionEn: Rich, oily or greasy in texture, or excessively flattering in manner.
example: The unctuous sauce coated the pasta in a rich buttery glaze.

definitionEn: Devoted to luxury and sensual pleasure, especially in food and comfort.
example: The sybaritic weekend included lavish dinners and long afternoons of wine.

definitionEn: A person who takes great pleasure in fine food, wine and refined living.
example: The epicurean critic travelled far to sample the region's rarest cheeses.

definitionEn: Relating to a meal, especially to dining or dinner conversation.
example: The guests enjoyed a lively prandial conversation over the long table.

definitionEn: To deliberately avoid or abstain from something.
example: The chef eschewed processed sugar and used honey to sweeten every dessert.

definitionEn: Extremely hungry, eager to eat large quantities of food.
example: After the long hike, the ravenous children devoured every sandwich in sight.

definitionEn: Eating greedily in large amounts, or having an insatiable appetite for something.
example: The voracious reader finished three novels during our short holiday.

definitionEn: Greedy and excessive eating or drinking.
example: Gluttony at the banquet left several guests feeling sick and sluggish.

definitionEn: Careful with money and food, using resources economically and avoiding waste.
example: The frugal family cooked simple meals and rarely wasted a single grain of rice.

definitionEn: Unwilling to spend or use more than necessary, often in a stingy way.
example: The parsimonious host served only one small biscuit per guest.

definitionEn: Plentiful, generous and abundant, especially in harvests or supplies.
example: The bountiful orchard produced more fruit than the village could possibly eat.

definitionEn: Generous in amount, or extremely rich and luxurious.
example: The newlyweds hosted a lavish feast with dishes from every region.

definitionEn: Rich, lavish and expensive, especially in food or furnishing.
example: The sumptuous banquet included roast goose, truffles and vintage champagne.

definitionEn: Pleasingly tasty or appetising, especially in food.
example: The toothsome dumplings disappeared from the platter within minutes.

definitionEn: A small piece or bite of food.
example: She offered a tiny morsel of cake to each of the children.

definitionEn: An item of food, especially one considered particularly delicious or choice.
example: The feast offered a generous array of viands from every corner of the realm.

definitionEn: Something that is fit to be eaten, usually as a food item.
example: The shop stocked a range of comestibles from local farms and bakers.

definitionEn: Food and provisions, especially stored for a journey or long period.
example: The travellers loaded their wagons with provender before crossing the desert.

definitionEn: A meal or the food served at a meal, especially a formal one.
example: The family gathered around the table for a simple but joyful repast.

definitionEn: A large formal meal for many guests, often held to celebrate an occasion.
example: The king hosted a grand banquet to welcome the visiting ambassadors.

definitionEn: A clear, thin broth made by simmering meat or vegetables in water.
example: She sipped a steaming cup of beef bouillon on the cold winter evening.

definitionEn: A rich stew of meat or vegetables cooked slowly in a well-flavoured sauce.
example: The ragout simmered gently all afternoon, filling the house with rich aromas.

definitionEn: Cured or smoked meat products, such as sausages, ham and pâté.
example: The platter of charcuterie featured thin slices of salami and country pâté.

definitionEn: A mixture of fat and flour cooked together to thicken a sauce or soup.
example: Stir the roux slowly until it turns golden before adding the milk.

definitionEn: Cut into thin, matchstick-sized strips, used especially for vegetables.
example: The chef cut the carrots into fine julienne for the garnish.

meaningVi: hỗn hợp rau củ cắt hạt lựu
definitionEn: A mixture of diced onions, carrots and celery used as a base for flavouring dishes.
example: Start the sauce by softening a mirepoix in butter for ten minutes.

definitionEn: A water bath in which dishes are gently heated or kept warm without boiling.
example: Place the custard dish in a bain-marie to cook it gently and evenly.

meaningVi: nấu chân không ở nhiệt độ thấp
definitionEn: Cooked in vacuum-sealed bags in a precisely controlled warm water bath.
example: The sous-vide salmon was tender and moist throughout its thickness.

definitionEn: Cooked until still firm when bitten, used especially of pasta.
example: The pasta was cooked al dente, firm to the bite but never hard.

definitionEn: To loosen browned food from a pan by adding liquid and stirring over heat.
example: Deglaze the pan with a splash of wine to capture every flavourful bit.

definitionEn: Served with alcohol set alight so that a flame flashes briefly over the dish.
example: The waiter prepared a flambé dessert with brandy at the table.

definitionEn: A bitter, astringent compound found in tea, wine and oak wood.
example: The tannin in the strong black tea gave it a drying finish.

definitionEn: The natural environment, soil and climate that give a food or wine its character.
example: The wine's distinctive character reflects the unique terroir of the hillside vineyard.

definitionEn: A drink taken before a meal to stimulate the appetite.
example: Before dinner, the guests gathered on the terrace for a chilled aperitif.
